Bill.BriefDescription: Creating a committee to evaluate high occupancy toll lanes.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to high occupancy toll lanes; adding new sectionsto chapter 47.56 RCW; creating a new section; and providing acontingent effective date.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BillSection.RCWSLText: It is the intent of the legislature toevaluate the feasibility of toll lanes, including high occupancy tolllanes, for new and replacement vehicle capacity on Interstate 405,state route 520, and the section of state route 99 known as the AlaskanWay Viaduct. The Interstate 405 study shall examine both currentlyfunded and proposed projects.

A high occupancy toll lanes steeringcommittee is hereby established to coordinate the feasibility studyactivity. Members of the high occupancy toll lanes steering committeeare to include regional planning organizations and stakeholder groups.

(1) Funding shall be provided to obtainindependent expert consultancy services to conduct the toll lanes p. 1 SB 6017feasibility studies. Evaluation criteria shall at a minimum include,but not be limited to: (a) Reduction in person and goods delay during peak periods,defined as 6 to 9 a.m. and 3 to 7 p.m.; (b) Revenue generation; (c) Use of revenues generated for transit and trip reductionprograms; (d) Ability of multioccupant vehicles to maintain fortyfive milesper hour minimum speed; and (e) The ability to incorporate freight needs. (2) Results of the feasibility study shall be delivered to thehouse and senate transportation committees of the legislature and thetransportation commission not later than December 1, 2005.
Sections 2 and 3 of this act are each addedto chapter 47.56 RCW.

This act takes effect August 1, 2005, ifspecific funding for the purposes of this act, referencing this act bybill or chapter number, is provided by June 30, 2005, in thetransportation appropriations act. If specific funding is not providedby June 30, 2005, this act is null and void.
